Short Black Opera continues to focus on the development of Indigenous opera singers through various programs and events. •	SBO supported the presentation of Deborah Cheetham’s new work, Eumeralla, a war requiem for peace, performed by the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra at Hamer Hall, Melbourne, in June 2019. Members of Dhungala Children’s Choir performed, along with soloists Deborah Cheetham AO, Don Bemrose and Linda Barcan to a soldout audience. “Eumeralla” will contribute to the growing understanding of Australia’s resistance wars and their impact on both Indigenous and nonIndigenous Australians and will provide ongoing development and training for Short Black Opera company members. •	Dhungala Children’s Choir, an Indigenous children’s choir, continued to rehearse and perform throughout the year, with members of the choir based in Shepparton and Geelong. The choir performed at the Dhungala Kaeila Oration in Shepparton in August, 2019 and have been involved in the creation of a new children’s opera, Cheeky Opera, due for release in 2020.•	Short Black Opera’s Dhungala Choral Connection Song Book was featured as part of the Boite School’s Chorus program in 2019, with over 1,000 children throughout Victoria learning 10 songs featuring Indigenous languages and performing them in concerts in Melbourne, Ballarat and Albury/Wodonga.•	SBO supported a presentation of Eumeralla, a war requiem for peace performed by students in the choir and orchestra of the University of Queensland, in Brisbane, October 2019. Members of Dhungala Children’s Choir and their families travelled to Brisbane for the performance, along with soloists Deborah Cheetham, Don Bemrose and Linda Barcan.•	Dhungala Children’s Choir presented a performance at the opening of the 2019 MPavilion in Melbourne, November, 2019 and at Wallace Lodge in Geelong, December 2019.  •	Short Black Opera continued its international presence with two tours overseas as part of the Woven Song series, featuring musical responses composed by Deborah Cheetham AO based on 9 tapestries featuring Indigenous works in Australian Embassies around the world. In March 2019, SBO toured to Mumbai and New Delhi with Rubiks Collective, working with Indian tabla master Pandit Ashis Sangupta in performances at the Royal Opera House Mumbai and the Australian Embassy’s residence in New Delhi. In April, SBO toured to Tokyo with Plexus Ensemble for a performance at the Australian Embassy, featuring Japanese Shakahachi master Reison Kuroda. This series will continue in 2020, with performances in Beijing with Orchestra Victoria and Italy with Melbourne Symphony Orchestra.

Sharing meetings for bereaved parents allow parents, (and grandparents and siblings) to talk about their losses in a safe and supported environment, thereby sharing their grief in a constructive and helpful manner. These books are available for loan by parents and their families.The Compassionate Friends offer friendship and support by organising regular events such as morning teas, lunches, dinners and craft days to encourage members to come together in a social setting. We always recognise the difficulties that can be associated with the family focussed times of the year such as Mothers Day, Fathers Day, Christmas and Easter. These social activities assist the welfare and general mental wellbeing of members.As a peer support organisation, all members have suffered a loss and offer understanding and support in how these events can affect everyone in a family.We have members who have attended Bereavement Network Support meetings to further the promotion of our group, are listed in local service directories and have distributed our chapter's pamphlet to numerous places including Dr's surgeries, funeral directors, COTA, palliative care providers, counselling services (school counselors, coronial counselling service, grief resource centre). Uni Camp for Kids is WA’s oldest registered children’s charity, continuing to achieve our aims of providing Camps and Picnics for emotionally, socially, and/or financially underprivileged Perth Children since 1936. The organisation, based at UWA, is run and staffed entirely by student volunteers. We run four daylong Picnics throughout the year, and three weeklong Summer Camps (in January) that are provided completely free to the children and their families, thanks to our fundraising efforts and our volunteers. Our mission is to saturate our event itineraries with fun and rewarding activities that take a proactive step towards improving the mindset and lives of atrisk children that their various circumstances often deprive them of. As we deal with kids in the most difficult circumstances, we prioritise a positive space for kids to be themselves above any agenda. Unlike other charities, we don't have any specific academic or behavioural outcomes for the kids. We instead provide a safe, carefree environment where they are able to experience constructive role modelling and create positive childhood memories. We also provide much needed respite to the families and carers of these children. Uni Camp is also beneficial to the student volunteers as a way of exposing students to a fun, rewarding volunteering experience.
